# Facet coincidences at a minimizing cap: an exact zonoid condition

This is an additional necessary condition, not an OC inequality. It
also strengthens the allocation quantifier in the two recent stress
notes. All statements below concern positive d-dimensional fibers,
d>=1, and their sum of d-dimensional volume.

## 1. The directional cap derivative

Let y be interior to one positive fiber, and let an ambient nonvertical
closed halfspace H have boundary through y and attain the depth at y.
Normalize its continuous normal v to length one. Write the full
physical variable as w=(p,x), and change the cap normal by t e while
moving its threshold by t e.y. Thus the moving cap continues to pass
through exactly y; on its original plane the margin velocity is

    ell(w)=e.(w-y).

For each fiber, classify its intersection with the cap plane as:

* a proper section cutting the fiber interior;
* an inside supporting facet, where the entire fiber lies in H;
* an outside supporting facet, where the cap has zero fiber volume;
* a section of zero (d-1)-measure, which contributes zero.

Let theta_P, theta_I, theta_O be the sums of H_(d-1) over these proper,
inside, and outside pieces, respectively. For d=1 they are H_0 sums
of section points. Put v(w)=w-y and m=integral v(w)dtheta_P(w).

The one-sided derivative of cap mass is exactly

    g(e)= e.m +integral min(0,e.v(w))dtheta_I(w)
                  +integral max(0,e.v(w))dtheta_O(w).              (1)

On a proper cut this is the ordinary slab formula, with unit continuous
normal. At a supporting facet the fixed body has normal velocity zero,
so the swept thickness is respectively min(0,ell) or max(0,ell).
The lower-dimensional intersections have zero area. Uniform bounded
displacement and the vanishing boundary area of shrinking neighborhoods
away from the listed facets justify summing the formulas, as in the
general boundary variation note. No cap-plane volume mass occurs,
because the continuous normal is nonzero.

Since H minimizes cap mass among all halfspaces through y, g(e)>=0
for every e, including both signs. Scaling the normal causes no extra
constraint: all vectors w-y in (1) lie in its plane, so a component
parallel to the original full normal has zero pairing there.

## 2. An exact inclusion of compact convex moment sets

For a finite compactly supported measure theta on the cap plane define

    Z(theta)={integral alpha(w)(w-y)dtheta(w):
                           alpha Borel, 0<=alpha<=1}.

This set is compact and convex. For example use weak-* compactness of
the bounded densities and the finitely many continuous coordinate
moments. Its support function is exactly

    h_(Z(theta))(e)=integral max(0,e.(w-y))dtheta(w),               (2)

with the maximum attained by the indicator of the positive scalar
product. Formula (1) and g(e)>=0 for all e are therefore equivalent to

    -Z(theta_I) subset m+Z(theta_O).                              (3)

Indeed (1) says h_(-Z(theta_I))(e)<=h_(m+Z(theta_O))(e) for every e;
compact convex sets satisfy this support inequality exactly when the
stated inclusion holds, by separation of any excluded point.

Equivalently, for EVERY prescribed inside density alpha_I in [0,1],
there exists an outside density alpha_O in [0,1] such that

    m+integral alpha_I(w)(w-y)dtheta_I
      +integral alpha_O(w)(w-y)dtheta_O=0.                        (4)

This is a universal quantifier on inside allocations. It is stronger
than merely asserting that some pair of densities centers the section.
It is an exact consequence of local minimizing-cap geometry, with no
smoothness or polyhedrality assumption on the fibers.

Adding (1) for e and -e also gives the useful necessary comparison

    integral |e.(w-y)|dtheta_I
                     <=integral |e.(w-y)|dtheta_O                (5)

for every full ambient vector e. This is a comparison of the indicated
absolute first moments. It is not asserted to imply arbitrary convex
order or second-moment domination.

## 3. An inside tangency requires an outside tangency

If theta_O=0, (3) forces Z(theta_I) to be a singleton. It contains zero,
so it is {0}, and (3) then gives m=0. Applying (5) to a coordinate basis
shows w=y theta_I-almost everywhere. But an inside supporting facet
cannot be in the own fiber, because y is interior to that fiber. In
every other fiber its base coordinate differs from y's. Hence w!=y
throughout every inside supporting facet. Therefore theta_I=0.

Consequently a depth-attaining cap which has no outside facet
coincidences has no inside facet coincidences either. Its ordinary
proper-section centroid is exactly y, since m=0 and the own proper
section supplies positive total area. This statement includes d=1.

## 4. Stronger quantifier for the body-variation stress

In `candidate a68c14b477a24d06`, an inside
coincident facet contributes min(r,ell), where r is body normal velocity
and ell is cap margin velocity. For EVERY fixed Borel alpha in [0,1],

    min(r,ell)<=alpha r+(1-alpha)ell.                (6)

Thus the robust separation proof can be run after prescribing in
advance ANY such alpha on EVERY inside cap/facet coincidence. Keep
those allocations fixed; allow variable outside allocations only,
because max(r+ell,0)=sup_(0<=alpha<=1) alpha(r+ell).

The reduced gradient sets are still compact convex on every finite
parameter space. Common erosion is strictly negative on all of them
because the own proper cap retains a positive strictly-inside boundary
patch. The signed joint homothety still gives dQ in every gradient,
since r=ell at an inside coincidence, regardless of the prescribed
alpha. Therefore all separation, normalization, and finite-intersection
steps go through unchanged.

The strengthened conclusion is: for EVERY selected critical cover and
EVERY prescribed system of inside-facet allocations, there exists a
normalized multiplier certificate and outside-facet allocations such
that the boundary source is below the full boundary measure in convex
order. The multiplier certificate can depend on the prescribed inside
allocations. It is not permissible to exchange these quantifiers and
demand one multiplier vector for all incompatible prescribed choices.

The same strengthening holds in
`candidate beffb23a92dd631a`. There the body is
fixed, so an inside branch is min(0,ell)<=sigma ell for every prescribed
sigma in [0,1]. Fixing those sigma values leaves the strict uniform
density-decrease direction and the normalization sum lambda=1/beta
unchanged. Its bulk moment certificate therefore has the same universal
inside-allocation quantifier.

These stronger necessary conditions have not been converted to the
numerical OC bound. They prevent loss of available concave-branch
information in subsequent audits of candidate arguments.
